parameters.typical: −1 for a command that can also brake or reverse, 0 for one that cannot; in the unit of what the output drives.
parameters.whereToFind: The range the input it feeds takes (a Traction Command runs from −1 to 1).

parameters.label: Output Maximum
parameters.description: The highest the output may go: it is held there when it would go higher.
parameters.typical: 1 for a command; in the unit of what the output drives.
parameters.whereToFind: The range the input it feeds takes.

parameters.label: Sample Time (0 = solver step)
parameters.description: How often the controller runs; its output holds in between, as in a real controller. 0, or any time shorter than the solver step (at most 10 ms), runs it every solver step.
parameters.typical: 0 for most models; 0.01–0.1 s to copy a real controller's cycle time (above 0.1 s Data Checks warn).
parameters.whereToFind: The real controller's cycle time.

components.name: Lookup Table
components.description: Applies a 1D or 2D lookup table to its input signal(s) — no-code signal shaping (e.g. pedal maps, recuperation weighting).

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: 1D: the output is the 1D Table read at Input X. 2D: the output is the 2D Table read at Input X and Input Y.
parameters.typical: 1D for a pedal map or a curve; 2D when the output depends on two signals, such as speed and SOC.
parameters.whereToFind: Your control strategy.

parameters.label: 1D Table
parameters.description: The output at each value of Input X. Between points it follows a straight line; outside them it holds the edge value, unless the table's outside-the-data setting says otherwise.
parameters.typical: A few points, such as a pedal map from 0 to 1.
parameters.whereToFind: Your strategy or a measured curve, typed or pasted from a spreadsheet into the table editor (Edit…).

parameters.label: 2D Table
parameters.description: The output at each pair of Input X and Input Y. Between points it is interpolated; outside them it holds the edge value, unless the table's outside-the-data setting says otherwise.
parameters.typical: A small grid, such as 5 × 5 points.
parameters.whereToFind: Your strategy or measured data, typed or pasted from a spreadsheet into the table editor (Edit…).

parameters.label: Sample Time (0 = solver step)
parameters.description: How often the block reads its table; its output holds in between, as in a real controller. 0, or any time shorter than the solver step (at most 10 ms), reads it every solver step.
parameters.typical: 0 for most models; 0.01–0.1 s to copy a real controller's cycle time (above 0.1 s Data Checks warn).
parameters.whereToFind: The real controller's cycle time.

components.name: Road Profile
components.description: Road grade profile over distance (or time), piecewise-linear 'x:grade%' pairs. Wire the grade output to the Vehicle's Road Grade input; in distance mode it follows the Vehicle's distance automatically when unwired.

parameters.label: Profile (x:grade%; …)
parameters.description: The road's grade over distance (m) or time (s) as 'x:grade' pairs separated by ';', grade in % (rise ÷ run × 100, uphill positive). Between points it follows a straight line; after the last it holds.
parameters.typical: Motorways up to about 5 % · mountain roads up to 10–12 % · steep city streets 15–20 %.
parameters.whereToFind: An elevation profile from a map service or a GPS log (grade = rise ÷ distance × 100), or the road's design data.

parameters.label: Profile Axis
parameters.description: Distance: x is the distance the Vehicle has driven, in m, or the Distance input when it is wired. Time: x is the time, in s.
parameters.typical: Distance for a route, so the hills stay where they are whatever the speed; time to replay a logged drive.
parameters.whereToFind: How your grade data is laid out: against distance (a map, a route) or against time (a log).

parameters.label: Repeat Profile
parameters.description: Ticked: after its last point the profile starts again from its first. Unticked: the last grade holds.
parameters.typical: Unticked for a route driven once; ticked for a closed track driven lap after lap.
parameters.whereToFind: Your route.

components.name: Race Track
components.description: The line a lap case (case Kind: Lap) drives: its curvature against distance (1/radius; + turns left, − right) and its elevation. A lap case finds the fastest speed along it about every metre, as a quasi-steady-state lap simulation does: in each corner the speed the tyres' lateral grip allows (with the Vehicle's downforce and load transfer, and each Wheel's load sensitivity), then full acceleration out of it and the latest braking into the next, within the tyres' friction ellipse, the E-Motors' full-load curves through the gears and the battery's deliverable power and Output Power Limit. The motors, gears, brakes and battery then drive that speed trace through the same models as a drive cycle, for the energy and the channels. The results are estimates for an ideal driver on the given line: no transients, suspension, yaw or tyre slip, and ideal brake balance. Only E-Motor drivelines: a lap case refuses Combustion Engines and Clutches, holds Gearboxes in their gear and commands the motors itself. Layouts drawn for LightSim, not official layouts: Autocross, a 979 m closed lap (straights up to 78 m, a slalom on 10 m cones, corners of 6 m radius or more, 3 sectors); Skidpad, a right then a left circle on the lane centre, 9.125 m radius (with 2 laps, lap 2's Sector 1 and Sector 2 are the timed right and left circles); Acceleration 75 m, an open straight. They follow Formula Student Rules 2026 v1.1 (FSG) D 4.1, D 5.1.1, D 6.1 and D 7.1; FSUK and FSAE may differ, check the current season's rules. Custom uses the Curvature and Elevation tables (paste them from a spreadsheet; from a logged lap, curvature = lateral acceleration / speed², smoothed), Closed Circuit and the Sector Ends. Lap 1 starts at the Vehicle's Initial Speed (no faster than its first corner allows), each later lap at the speed the one before ended with. The Limit channel says what held the car back: 1 cornering grip, 2 traction grip, 3 motor, 4 battery, 5 Output Power Limit, 6 braking. The case's Duration, Step and Pacing do not apply to lap cases; its Store every does.

parameters.label: Layout
parameters.description: The line a lap case drives: Autocross, a 979 m closed lap; Skidpad, a right and then a left circle of 9.125 m radius; Acceleration 75 m, an open straight; or Custom, from the Curvature and Elevation tables. The layouts are drawn for LightSim, not official ones.
parameters.typical: Autocross for a lap time or the endurance energy · Skidpad for cornering grip · Acceleration 75 m to compare with an acceleration case · Custom for your own track.
parameters.whereToFind: Your event: the layouts follow FS Rules 2026 v1.1 (FSG) D 4.1, D 5.1.1, D 6.1 and D 7.1. For a real track, Custom with the curvature from a logged lap or a map.

parameters.label: Laps
parameters.description: How many laps a lap case drives, one after the other: lap 1 from the Vehicle's Initial Speed (no faster than the first corner allows), each later lap from the speed the one before ended with. A lap case sets it among its own values.
parameters.typical: 1 for a standing lap · 2 for a flying lap (the Lap time is the fastest) · about 22 for a Formula Student endurance on a 1 km lap (the FS example 23).
parameters.whereToFind: The event's distance ÷ the lap length (a Formula Student endurance is about 22 km).

parameters.label: Curvature (Custom)
parameters.description: The Custom track's curvature (1 ÷ radius) at each distance along the line: positive turns left, negative right, 0 is straight. It must start at 0 m, be at least 10 m long and bend no tighter than 0.5 1/m (a 2 m radius).
parameters.typical: 0 on straights · 0.1 1/m in a corner of 10 m radius, 0.03 1/m in one of about 33 m.
parameters.whereToFind: A logged lap (lateral acceleration ÷ speed², smoothed) or a map (1 ÷ each corner's radius), pasted from a spreadsheet into the table editor (Edit…).

parameters.label: Elevation (Custom)
parameters.description: The Custom track's height at each distance along it, in m. Its slope makes the car climb and descend, as a road grade does. Beyond its last point the height holds.
parameters.typical: 0 m everywhere (the default) for a flat track, as most Formula Student tracks are; a few metres over a lap on a hilly circuit.
parameters.whereToFind: A GPS log's altitude against distance, a map's elevation profile, or the circuit's own data.

parameters.label: Closed Circuit (Custom)
parameters.description: Ticked: the Custom track is a circuit whose end joins its start, so each lap brakes for the next lap's first corner; Data Checks warn when its curvature does not turn it back to its start. Unticked: an open stretch, such as a sprint.
parameters.typical: Ticked for a circuit; unticked for a straight or a hill climb.
parameters.whereToFind: Your track.

parameters.label: Sector Ends (Custom, m; …)
parameters.description: Where each sector of the Custom track ends, in m from the start, separated by ';'; the last sector ends at the finish. The summary gives each sector's time on the fastest lap. Empty: one sector.
parameters.typical: Empty, or two or three ends such as '280; 630' (the Autocross layout's).
parameters.whereToFind: The timing points of your event or circuit.
